hotel_name: Eros Hotel New Delhi Nehru Place

positive_snippets:
I stayed at this hotel as a solo traveler with the Gate 1 tour group, and from the moment I walked in until the moment I left, I was treated like gold! My room was beautiful, spacious, and spotless, with a clean bathroom stocked with plenty of amenities in case you forget anything.

I loved that the TV had access to Netflix, Hulu, and Disney+, which made it easy to unwind after a long day of touring. The breakfast buffet offered a great variety of options, and while I’m a picky eater, I appreciated the made-to-order eggs — they were perfect.

Overall, I was extremely pleased with my stay and would absolutely recommend this hotel to anyone looking for comfort, great service, and a welcoming atmosphere.

The hotel staff is wonderful. The breakfast buffet has something for everyone. The location is near shops and an ATM. The rooms are a bit worn, but comfortable. If you are a light sleeper, bring ear plugs the doors are very heavy and because of the stone floors when someone leaves their room the doors slam very loudly.

Very beautifully decorated currently for Christmas. Love the Pan-Asian, all time favourite and indian (Singh Sahab). Delicious food. Very helpful staff, and polite. Love the golden fried prawns, kung-pao chicken, the chicken Biryani, galauti kebabs, the dry fruit naan (peshawari naan), and so much more.
negative_snippets:
I'm writing this from Room #702, on the last of what has been an incredibly disappointing three-night stay (7th–10th October 2025). And honestly, I couldn’t be more relieved to be checking out.

At first glance, the hotel tries to impress with an old-world charm — but don't be fooled. Beneath the vintage veneer lies a crumbling, outdated property that seems stuck in a time warp. Everything feels aged beyond comfort, and not in a charming, nostalgic way — in a neglected, worn-out, why-is-this-still-operating sort of way.

The location? Smack in the middle of Nehru Place, one of the busiest electronics markets in Delhi. That means relentless honking, chaotic traffic, and a soundtrack of city noise that follows you right into your room, day and night. If sleep is what you're after, prepare for a battle.

But the real horror show began when I was first given a room on the 4th floor. The moment I stepped out of the elevator, I was hit by the overpowering stench of stale cigarette smoke — the entire floor reeked like an old ashtray. This, after I’d clearly requested a non-smoking room and was told I had one. I informed the front desk I would cancel my entire stay if not shifted immediately. Only then was I grudgingly moved to the 7th floor.

But the worst — and I mean truly revolting — moment came during breakfast. I asked for a simple black coffee. What I received was served in a mug so filthy, it could have been pulled out of a dumpster. Sticky residue coated the inside and outside, and mysterious debris floated in the coffee itself. I showed it to the staff, expecting outrage, urgency — anything. Their response? A casual, "Sorry, let me get you another coffee." No concern, no apology worth the name. Honestly, it was a health hazard in plain sight.

For the price they’re charging, this place is a joke. The service is apathetic, the hygiene appalling, and the ambiance far from what a five-star experience should be. There are far better hotels in Delhi — cleaner, quieter, and infinitely more professional.

Today, as I pack my bags, I leave not just disappointed, but genuinely baffled that this hotel dares to call itself a luxury property.

It is a pretty average hotel- aspires to be world class but not so.
Great location
The current management must work with Hyatt Taj ITC etc to get best in class processes
